item.title: Alembic Pharma receives USFDA approval for lung cancer drug Binimetinib
item.description: Alembic Pharmaceuticals has received final approval from the US Food and Drug Administration for its Abbreviated New Drug Application for Binimetinib tablets for treatment of lung cancer. The approved Abbreviated New Drug Application (ANDA) is therapeutically equivalent to the reference listed drug product, Mektovi Tablets (15 mg), of Array BioPharma Inc, the company said in a regulatory filing on Saturday. Alembic is eligible for 180 days of generic drug exclusivity for Binimetinib Tablets, 15 mg and 45 mg, as it was one of the first ANDA applicants for the 15 mg strength and the sole first applicant for the 45 mg strength to submit a substantially complete ANDA with a paragraph IV certification, the filing said. Binimetinib is a kinase inhibitor indicated, in combination with encorafenib, for the treatment of patients with unresectable or metastatic melanoma and non-small cell lung cancer with a BRAF V600E mutation, it said. item.title: ONGC takes over disputed Cambay block from Vedanta after court ruling
item.description: State-run Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) has taken over operations and control of the disputed Cambay offshore block from Vedanta Oil & Gas Ltd following a Delhi High Court ruling, according to regulatory filings by the two companies. Vedanta Oil & Gas Ltd has recognised an impairment charge of about Rs 379 crore against assets and receivables linked to the block. The takeover of the CB-OS-02 block took effect on July 22, 2026, after the High Court's single-judge bench dismissed Vedanta's challenge to the government's decision not to extend the production-sharing contract, ONGC said in its quarterly filing. The block was operated by Vedanta, which held a 40 per cent participating interest; ONGC held 50 per cent, and Invenire Petrodyne Ltd had the remaining 10 per cent. The government, through a September 19, 2025, letter, declined to extend the contract and directed the operator to hand over the block to ONGC. Vedanta challenged the decision before the Delhi High Court

item.title: From bicycle parts to satellites: Inside Sunil Mittal's 50-year journey
item.description: When Sunil Bharti Mittal set up a small manufacturing unit making bicycle parts in Ludhiana in 1976, he was barely 18. Fifty years later, the founder of Bharti Enterprises is presiding over a business empire whose flagship, Bharti Airtel, has become one of the world's largest telecommunications companies. The journey from bicycle crankshafts to mobile networks, submarine cables and satellite communications has been marked by bets that often ran ahead of the market, setbacks triggered by policy changes and three major crises that Mittal describes as Bharti's "Mahabharatas". Now, as the group marks its 50th anniversary, Mittal is preparing for another transformation. item.title: Listing may change 'Tata way', put profits ahead of philanthropy: Noel
item.description: Tata Trusts Chairman Noel Tata on Saturday said that listing Tata Sons will "fundamentally change" the over 150-year-old group's way of working and stressed that its largest owner will play a "constructive role" in engaging with the regulators to retain the conglomerate's unlisted character. Speaking at the Hindustan Times Leadership Summit here, Noel said while "some people" are proposing a listing for the group's holding company, he fears that enlarging the number of shareholders after a listing will shift its focus to profits from philanthropy. "My worry is that listing, which is what some people are proposing, will change the Tata way. And one day, if we have 30,000-40,000 shareholders, profit may take precedence over philanthropy. And I think that will fundamentally change the Tata way of working," Noel, who turned 70 on Friday, was quoted as saying.
